businessContext.companyDescription: Homage (homage.com) is an e-commerce brand operating on Shopify Plus with NetSuite as their ERP. They sell through their own storefront and via EDI to licensed-apparel retailers including Fanatics, Dick's Sporting Goods, and Rallyhouse. They run a meaningful in-house engineering stack on AWS. They are currently evaluating iPaaS vendors to replace Celigo.

businessContext.competitiveContext: Active vendor evaluation — 3 to 4 iPaaS vendors in consideration. DataSkate is not the only platform being assessed.

p0Flags.gotcha: REST API requires PS256 JWT via Java helper library
p0Flags.clientAction: Confirm whether NetSuite REST API or RESTlet API is in use. If REST API: ensure the Java-based JWT signing helper is available and MuleSoft deployment can execute it (CloudHub 2.0 supports Java, but confirm).
p0Flags.architectNote: NetSuite REST API requires JWT signed with PS256 algorithm, which requires a Java helper library — not natively supported by DataWeave alone. NetSuite RESTlet alternative uses NLAuth/OAuth 1.0a. Celigo likely used RESTlet or a pre-built adapter. Confirm which auth method Celigo uses today and whether client has admin access to NetSuite integration records.

p0Flags.gotcha: EDI transactions 810, 856, 997 require B2B EDI connector, ACK/NACK handling, and trading partner registry
p0Flags.clientAction: Confirm whether Orderful ↔ NetSuite EDI is in scope for the new iPaaS. If yes: MuleSoft B2B EDI connector (X12) is required — confirm license. Define ACK/NACK handling and partner registry setup for Fanatics, DSG, Rallyhouse.
p0Flags.architectNote: Orderful is a cloud EDI gateway that typically exposes a REST API for receiving/sending EDI documents. MuleSoft can connect via HTTP to Orderful's API OR via direct AS2/X12 depending on setup. If direct X12 is needed: MuleSoft B2B X12 connector required. Orderful may abstract this to REST — Vera/Rex to confirm Orderful API model. Not currently a Celigo-managed flow.

p0Flags.gotcha: SOQL OFFSET does not apply (Shopify, not Salesforce) — but Shopify pagination cursor pattern required for bulk fetches
p0Flags.clientAction: Confirm approach for bulk data fetches (full sync scenarios). Shopify REST API uses cursor-based pagination; Shopify GraphQL uses connection/edges pattern. The Shopify MuleSoft connector handles this but configuration varies.
p0Flags.architectNote: Shopify Plus connector v1.x supports REST API; GraphQL Admin API is the modern approach for bulk operations. Matrix item product catalog size may require paginated bulk reads. Confirm with Kailash which connector version was used on prior Shopify engagements.

p0Flags.gotcha: Custom JavaScript transformations (pre-map, post-response, post-submit hooks) must be ported to DataWeave
p0Flags.clientAction: Request access to all custom JS transformation code in Celigo before migration planning. Assess complexity per flow. Identify original developer — they hold context on business rules embedded in the transforms.
p0Flags.architectNote: Celigo custom JS hooks map to: pre-map → input transformation (DataWeave before connector call), post-response → response transformation (DataWeave after connector call), post-submit → async callback handling. Complexity ranges from simple field mapping to conditional logic. Cannot be auto-converted — manual DataWeave port required per flow. This is the primary migration effort driver.
